title: Barkjohn et al. (2021) -- US-wide PurpleAir Correction
summary: Raw PurpleAir overestimates PM2.5 by ~40%. Correction reduces RMSE from 8 to 3 ug/m3. Corrected sensors report accurate NowCast AQI 90% of the time (vs. 75% uncorrected).
thesis_relevance: Gold standard PurpleAir correction; DustBoy R2=0.909 outperforms most uncorrected PurpleAir values.

title: Jaffe et al. (2023) -- EPA Correction in Smoke/Dust Events
summary: Corrections accurate for smoke events but underestimate dust by 5-6x. High-concentration divergence above 300 ug/m3.
thesis_relevance: Thailand burning season creates smoke-dominated aerosol; validates correction approach for biomass burning context.

title: Barkjohn et al. (2022) -- Extreme Wildfire Smoke Correction
summary: 12 of 13 sensors met EPA targets post-correction. Nonlinear response at >300 ug/m3 addressed via quadratic fit.
thesis_relevance: DustBoy experiences PM2.5 up to 280 ug/m3 during burning season, right at the critical correction boundary.

title: Mahajan & Helbing (2025) -- Trust-Based Dynamic Calibration
journal: npj Climate and Atmospheric Science (Q1, IF ~9.0)
summary: 4-indicator trust framework (accuracy, stability, responsiveness, consensus). MAE reductions up to 68% for poor sensors, 35-38% for reliable ones.
thesis_relevance: HIGHEST CONCEPTUAL ALIGNMENT -- trust-scoring parallels DustBoy's A-F confidence grading. Nature-family validation of the confidence scoring concept.

title: Samae et al. (2025) -- DustBoy Precision and Accuracy
summary: DustBoy Pro/Nx precision within +/-10% at <100 ug/m3. Upward bias at >100 ug/m3. Sensor age affects accuracy. Model-specific correction equations developed.
thesis_relevance: ONLY published DustBoy validation paper. Must cite and extend -- thesis scales from 2 colocation periods to network-wide multi-year assessment.

title: Raheja et al. (2023) -- Multi-Brand Sensor Intercomparison, Accra
summary: After GMR correction: PurpleAir R2=0.86, QuantAQ R2=0.87. XGBoost best within training range but failed extrapolation.
thesis_relevance: DustBoy R2=0.909 exceeds all post-correction values. Validates developing-country sensor networks in top-tier journals.

title: Bulot et al. (2023) -- Reference-Grade from Low-Cost Sensors
summary: PMS5003 calibrated RMSE down to 3.0-3.1 ug/m3. Between-unit uncertainty ~1.1-1.2 ug/m3. Twice-yearly calibration recommended.
thesis_relevance: Same Plantower sensor family as DustBoy; demonstrates calibratable to reference-grade.

title: Mathieu-Campbell et al. (2024) -- PurpleAir under High RH
summary: SSC model R2=0.74, RMSE=2.94. 16-23% error reduction over Barkjohn. Nonlinear RH effect at 50% threshold.
thesis_relevance: Chiang Mai monsoon RH >80%; nonlinear PM2.5/RH relationship directly applicable to DustBoy seasonal behavior.

title: Patel et al. (2024) -- Hygroscopic Growth Calibration
summary: Kappa-Kohler theory applied to PMS5003. Seasonal kappa parameter; RMSE reduction ~40%.
thesis_relevance: Physical (not just statistical) basis for calibration; seasonal kappa adaptable for burning vs. monsoon aerosol.

title: Dejchanchaiwong et al. (2023) -- Seasonal Calibration in Thailand
summary: PMS7003 at 3 Thai sites. Low PM + high humidity reduced performance. Northern Thailand performed better than Bangkok in dry season.
thesis_relevance: CLOSEST published work to DustBoy thesis. Same country, sensor family, seasonal context. DustBoy thesis extends from 3 sites to 834.

title: Scientific Reports (2025) -- ML Mixed Correction
summary: ANN-based approach: R2=0.87 for PM2.5, RMSE 3.0-4.9 ug/m3.
thesis_relevance: DustBoy R2=0.909 exceeds this result -- publishable performance advantage.

title: npj (2025) -- Comprehensive Correction Comparison
journal: npj Climate and Atmospheric Science (Q1, IF ~9.0)
summary: Correction varies substantially by device and environment. Pre-calibrated correction is underexplored.
thesis_relevance: DustBoy's 5-factor grading is the multi-factor correction system this paper recommends.

title: npj (2024) -- ML for Large Networks, India
journal: npj Climate and Atmospheric Science (Q1, IF ~9.0)
summary: R2 improved to 0.996 (ATMOS) and 0.999 (PurpleAir) with Decision Tree.
thesis_relevance: Sets high bar for ML-calibrated performance; demonstrates what is achievable.

title: npj (2024) -- Field Calibration, Semi-Arid Mexico
journal: npj Climate and Atmospheric Science (Q1, IF ~9.0)
summary: XGBoost best: R2~0.5 in industrial semi-arid environment.
thesis_relevance: DustBoy R2=0.909 dramatically outperforms (R2~0.5), suggesting biomass-smoke environments are more favorable for sensor calibration.

title: Barkjohn et al. (2025) -- Long-Term Evaluation of Six Sensor Types
summary: 58 sensors, 6 models, 7 US sites, 18 months. PurpleAir R2=0.67-0.94. Common failures: zeros, false highs, baseline shift, RH influence.
thesis_relevance: ESSENTIAL benchmark for long-term performance. DustBoy's 2.6B records over years is longer. Exclusion rules directly address identified failure modes.

title: Levy Zamora et al. (2023) -- Optimal Colocation Periods
summary: Diminishing returns after ~6 weeks. 3 weeks sufficient for linear; 7-8 weeks for ML methods.
thesis_relevance: Informs required DustBoy-BAM colocation duration; thesis should verify seasonal cycle coverage.

title: Giordano et al. (2021) -- Best Practices Review
summary: Key decisions: reference type (BAM vs. TEOM), averaging interval, cross-validation strategy, colocation duration (min 3 weeks linear, 7-8 weeks ML). Particle composition is major confounder.
thesis_relevance: METHODOLOGY GUIDE -- every thesis methodology choice should be justified against these best-practice guidelines.

title: Clements et al. (2024) -- Sensor QA Expert Perspectives
journal: ACS ES&T Air (Q1, new ACS journal)
summary: EPA-hosted expert consensus on QAPPs for sensor data. Recommends batch testing, seasonal calibration, active sensor health monitoring.
thesis_relevance: FRAMEWORK VALIDATION -- DustBoy's 5-factor grading IS the QA framework this panel recommends.

title: deSouza et al. (2022) -- Network-Level Calibration
summary: Full-period models more accurate but impractical for continuous recalibration. On-the-fly corrections capture short-term drift.
thesis_relevance: DustBoy's 834+ sensors need network-level QA; this paper informs the approach.

title: Carotenuto et al. (2023) -- Network Review for Long-Term Campaigns
summary: Most networks in developed countries despite greater need in developing regions. Dense networks capture pollution hotspots missed by regulatory stations.
thesis_relevance: DustBoy fills the exact developing-country gap this review identifies.

title: Bai et al. (2024) -- LGHAP v2 Global Gap-Free Dataset
summary: PM2.5 validation R=0.95, RMSE=5.7 ug/m3 vs 350 holdout sites. Daily 1 km gap-free global coverage.
thesis_relevance: PRIMARY COMPARISON DATASET -- does R=0.95 global performance hold in Northern Thailand burning season?

title: Bai et al. (2022) -- LGHAP v1
summary: First gap-free 1 km PM2.5 dataset (China, 2000-2020). Foundation for v2 methodology.
thesis_relevance: Training data was predominantly Chinese stations -- may affect SE Asia accuracy.

title: Cho et al. (2024) -- First GEMS Aerosol Results
summary: AOD R=0.792 (raw), R=0.920 (post-correction). 52.93% met +/-0.1 uncertainty threshold.
thesis_relevance: Foundational GEMS accuracy paper. Raw GEMS underestimates high AOD, overestimates low AOD -- critical for burning season comparison.

title: Jang et al. (2025) -- GEMS AOD Validation over Mainland SEA
journal: Aerosol and Air Quality Research (Q2, IF ~3.9)
summary: Overall R2=0.75. Dry season R2=0.63-0.79. Rainy season R2 drops to 0.11-0.13. Distinct April AOD peak.
thesis_relevance: DIRECTLY validates GEMS over DustBoy's geographic domain. Seasonal accuracy collapse (dry ~0.75 vs wet ~0.12) is critical for interpreting DustBoy-vs-GEMS comparison.

title: O et al. (2025) -- GEMS AOD to Hourly PM2.5 via ML
summary: RF and XGBoost on GEMS AOD + meteorology for hourly PM2.5 in South Korea. Strong temporal/spatial capture.
thesis_relevance: Demonstrates pipeline from GEMS AOD to PM2.5 estimates; method adaptable for Northern Thailand.

title: Kim et al. (2020) -- GEMS Mission
summary: Foundational GEMS mission paper. First geostationary air quality satellite covering Asia.
thesis_relevance: Required citation for any work using GEMS data.

title: Wei et al. (2023) -- GlobalHighPM2.5 / GHAP
summary: Cross-validated R2=0.91, RMSE=9.2 ug/m3 daily. 96% of populated areas exceeded WHO 24h guideline at least once.
thesis_relevance: Alternative global PM2.5 product to LGHAP v2; secondary validation dataset.

title: van Donkelaar et al. (2021) -- WashU/ACAG SatPM2.5
summary: Spatial CV R2=0.92, temporal CV R2=0.85. Known bias in data-sparse tropical regions.
thesis_relevance: Most widely used satellite PM2.5 for health studies. DustBoy ground truth fills known tropical data gaps.

title: Li et al. (2022) -- CAMS and MERRA-2 Validation
summary: CAMS overestimates; MERRA-2 underestimates. Large spatially varying biases, especially in undermonitored regions.
thesis_relevance: Documents known biases in reanalysis products for multi-source comparison context.

title: Aman et al. (2024) -- Fengyun-4A Geostationary PM2.5, Bangkok
summary: Good agreement for hourly/monthly patterns. PM2.5 peaks 08-10 LT. Areas outside Bangkok higher due to biomass burning.
thesis_relevance: Thailand-specific geostationary satellite PM2.5; complements GEMS approach.

title: Tian et al. (2023) -- Review: Satellite PM2.5 Challenges
summary: 40-80% satellite AOD missing due to cloud/surface contamination. ML susceptible to error in data-sparse regions.
thesis_relevance: Documents why ground sensors like DustBoy are irreplaceable -- continuous data regardless of cloud cover.

title: npj (2023) -- Synergistic Ground + Geostationary Satellite
journal: npj Climate and Atmospheric Science (Q1, IF ~9.0)
summary: Geostationary hourly PM2.5 has mean bias of -21.4% (hourly), -15.3% (daily) vs ground observations.
thesis_relevance: BRIDGES THE GAP -- shows how ground sensors, satellites, and models combine; directly informs multi-source comparison framework.

title: AMT (2025) -- ML Data Fusion for High Spatio-Temporal PM2.5
summary: 3D U-Net producing hourly 100m x 100m PM2.5 maps. Multi-source integration outperforms any single source.
thesis_relevance: State-of-the-art fusion; DustBoy network could serve as ground input layer with LGHAP v2, GEMS, CAMS as satellite/model layers.

title: Shao et al. (2024) -- PM2.5 Dataset for Mekong River Basin
journal: Science of the Total Environment (Q1, IF ~9.8)
summary: CNN + LightGBM stacking: R2=0.913, RMSE=10.637 ug/m3. First continuous PM2.5 for entire Mekong Basin.
thesis_relevance: Same geographic domain as DustBoy. R2=0.91 regional benchmark. Can compare: do Grade A DustBoy sensors agree better than Grade C/D?

title: Bainomugisha et al. (2025) -- Low-Cost + Satellite in Kampala
journal: International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology (Q2, IF ~3.5)
summary: Dry R2=0.67, wet R2=0.55. Cloud cover during wet season degrades satellite AOD. Humidity affects low-cost sensors.
thesis_relevance: Paradigmatic study for using low-cost sensors as ground truth in data-sparse tropics -- exactly DustBoy's role.

title: npj (2025) -- Evolving Trends in Low-Cost Sensor Networks
journal: npj Climate and Atmospheric Science (Q1, IF ~9.0)
summary: Key trends: ML calibration, satellite data fusion, network-level QA, trust-based quality metrics. Developing country gap critical.
thesis_relevance: Positions DustBoy at intersection of multiple hot research trends.

title: Chansuebsri & Chantara (2024) -- PM2.5 Source Apportionment, Chiang Mai
summary: Average PM2.5 of 116+/-35 ug/m3 during smoke-haze. Biomass burning contributed 59.3 ug/m3 (dominant). Main source area: Thai-Myanmar border.
thesis_relevance: Definitive source apportionment for Chiang Mai. The 8x burning-to-monsoon ratio in DustBoy data is consistent with these findings.

title: Saksakulkrai & Chantara (2026) -- Molecular Markers, Northern Thailand
summary: Three distinct biomass burning sources: mixed (31%), local (19%), aged/transported (13%). Aged aerosols from mixed burning dominate episodic haze.
thesis_relevance: Aged vs. local aerosol distinction affects light-scattering sensor accuracy differently.

title: Inlaung et al. (2024) -- WRF-Chem Transboundary PM2.5
summary: Transboundary PM2.5 often surpasses local sources. Influx begins January, intensifies northward, peaks March.
thesis_relevance: Directly relevant to WRF-CHEM comparison component. Transboundary patterns explain spatial variation in DustBoy readings.

title: Thongsame et al. (2025) -- Source Attribution and Health Burden
summary: Foreign biomass burning = 23-38% of PM2.5. 4,240 mortality in Bangkok attributed to PM2.5.
thesis_relevance: WRF-Chem baseline for Thailand; explains border province vs. interior station differences.

title: WRF-Chem Emissions Evaluation (2024)
summary: CAMS-GLOB-ANT best for North Thailand; FINN1.5 best for biomass burning. Nighttime boundary layer errors significant.
thesis_relevance: Essential for selecting WRF-Chem configuration and weighting nighttime DustBoy readings.

title: Ponsawansong et al. (2023) -- Oxidative Potential, Chiang Mai
journal: Aerosol and Air Quality Research (Q2, IF ~3.6)
summary: Biomass burning = 57.9% of PM2.5 during haze. Secondary inorganic 26.2%, vehicles 7.8%.
thesis_relevance: Health-relevant context for why accurate PM2.5 monitoring during burning season is critical.

title: Kawichai et al. (2024) -- Carbonaceous Species, Chiang Mai
summary: Mean PM2.5 = 38.7 ug/m3. OC/EC = 7.71 confirms dominant biomass burning.
thesis_relevance: Carbonaceous composition explains seasonal accuracy differences in DustBoy light-scattering sensors.

title: Suriyawong et al. (2023) -- Biomass Burning Review, Thailand
summary: Comprehensive review of PM from biomass burning across all Thai regions. Northern Thailand dominated by forest/agricultural fires.
thesis_relevance: Broad Thai context for burning PM2.5. Authored by CMU colleagues (Phairuang, Samae, Suriyawong).

title: Amnuaylojaroen & Parasin (2023) -- Daily PM2.5 in Thailand, 1 km
summary: Random forest best for PM2.5 prediction from MODIS MAIAC AOD at 1 km over Thailand.
thesis_relevance: Thailand-specific satellite PM2.5 benchmark, directly comparable to DustBoy's 834 ground stations.

title: Amnuaylojaroen et al. (2023) -- RF PM2.5 in Northern Thailand
journal: Environmental Science and Pollution Research (Q2, IF ~5.8)
summary: RF at 3 km resolution over Northern Thailand. Captures burning season elevation.
thesis_relevance: Same region as highest DustBoy density. Grid-cell comparison with DustBoy possible.

title: Continuous PM2.5 Record, East Asia (2025)
summary: 12-year GOCI PM2.5 record at 2 km daily over East Asia. PM2.5 peaked 2013-2014 then declined.
thesis_relevance: Template for what a DustBoy + GEMS long-term record could achieve for SE Asia.

title: Jarernwong et al. (2023a) -- Health Risk Map, DustBoy Data
summary: Correlations: PM2.5 vs dermatitis R=0.84, conjunctivitis R=0.81, stroke R=0.74, lung cancer R=0.73.
thesis_relevance: DustBoy data already used for health research -- validates importance of confidence scoring.

title: Jarernwong et al. (2023b) -- Health Impacts, Northern Thailand
summary: ~41,372 years of life lived with disability per 100,000 population annually from PM2.5 in northern Thailand.
thesis_relevance: Quantifies health stakes -- reliable DustBoy data is a public health necessity.

title: Jarernwong et al. (2021) -- Early DustBoy Health Mapping
summary: First study using DustBoy network data for systematic health mapping.
thesis_relevance: Early validation of DustBoy data utility, establishing need for quality assurance.

title: Taneepanichskuld et al. (2025) -- PM2.5 and Mortality, Thailand
journal: International Journal of Environmental Health Research (Q2, IF ~3.1)
summary: Significant PM2.5-mortality correlations. 6% increase in deaths during high-pollution periods. Stronger in central and northern provinces.
thesis_relevance: Links satellite PM2.5 (one comparison source) with mortality, validating multi-source monitoring accuracy.

title: Jainonthee et al. (2022) -- Respiratory Diseases, Chiang Mai
summary: 10-year analysis. PM2.5 and prior-month temperature predict influenza incidence. Clear seasonal patterns.
thesis_relevance: 10-year timeframe aligns with DustBoy long-term analysis.

title: Marvin et al. (2024) -- Biomass Burning Aerosol Uncertainty, SE Asia
summary: Monthly attributable deaths underestimated by up to 4,500 in March. Emission inventory uncertainties propagate to PM2.5 and health.
thesis_relevance: If satellite products rely on emission inventories for gap-filling, burning uncertainty directly affects their Thai accuracy. DustBoy provides independent verification.

title: Marks & Miller (2022) -- Political Ecology of Air Pollution
summary: Administrative fragmentation and elite interests compromise transboundary air governance.
thesis_relevance: Governance context for why citizen-science networks like DustBoy are essential. Confidence scoring makes citizen data credible.

title: Akahoshi et al. (2024) -- Open Burning Control Barriers
summary: Social/institutional barriers cause 2x PM2.5 emissions over 10-20 years. Cost ~$14M/year.
thesis_relevance: Monitoring networks like DustBoy needed to verify whether burning policies work.

title: Jainontee et al. (2023) -- PM2.5 Strategy, Northern Thailand
summary: Strategy framework incorporating monitoring, source control, and policy for Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai.
thesis_relevance: Reliable monitoring data is foundational to strategy design; DustBoy confidence scoring enables this.
